newsitem.title: USA: SRP seeks FERC action on Mexico transmission.
newsitem.headline: SRP seeks FERC action on Mexico transmission.

text.p: Salt River Project (SRP) will likely ask the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to look into the availability of pwoer transmission access into Mexico, the Phoenix, Ariz.-based public utility said Thursday.
The decision follows the collapse of talks with El Paso Electric Co over access to transmission from the Palo Verde substation in Arizona through to El Paso's interconnect with northern Mexico.

El Paso said it does not have enough surplus capacity to accomodate SRP's request and that SRP failed to account for the cost of ancillary services in its bid to Comision Federal de Electricidad (CFE), Mexico's national utility.
El Paso officials "clearly don't understand the spirit of the FERC rule" on open transmission access, said Lisa Urias, head of SRP's Mexico power group.
CFE will probably "be forced to go with El Paso, probably for the next year," she said. SRP has offered to sell CFE 6 MW of the total 200 MW contract for calendar 1997.
Urias said SRP will do "everything we can to assure this is the last year they have that monopoly."
She noted there obviously are constraints on El Paso's sytem, but SRP calculates there is space for 120 MW from Arizona.
SRP expects to monitor closely El Paso's transmission activity when the FERC-mandated OASIS system goes live in January.
The real time information system will allow utilities and other energy providers to find out about transmission prices and available capacity.
